use_cases.title: One assistant on every intranet site
use_cases.scenario: Employees open the intranet home, HR, IT or a project site and chat with the same company agent, already signed in.
use_cases.how: One tenant-wide SPFx package and one Entra SPA app serve every site. Each page stores only the agent's connection string.
use_cases.evidence: Agent A answered every shared tester on every site they could open (8 of 8 runs across Sites A, B and C).

use_cases.title: Only approved people can chat
use_cases.scenario: HR shares the HR agent with the HR team. Anyone else who opens the page is refused, on every site.
use_cases.how: Copilot Studio sharing (**End user access**) is enforced on every Agents SDK call. Use Entra security groups in production.
use_cases.evidence: Unshared users got *You don't have access to talk to this bot* on every site. Revoking and re-sharing took effect on the next page load.

use_cases.title: The agent knows who is chatting
use_cases.scenario: The agent greets employees by name and can use their identity in topics, for example to look up their own requests.
use_cases.how: With **Authenticate with Microsoft**, Copilot Studio receives the signed-in user, so `System.User.*` variables are filled in.
use_cases.evidence: Every greeting used the tester's name (`Hello Agents SDK User A!`). The web part footer shows the signed-in account.

use_cases.title: Single sign-on, also with MFA
use_cases.scenario: People already signed in to SharePoint start chatting without another prompt. If the browser blocks silent sign-in, one click fixes it.
use_cases.how: MSAL `acquireTokenSilent`, then `ssoSilent` with the SharePoint user as login hint. Fallback: **Sign in with Microsoft** popup; one sign-in serves every agent on the page.
use_cases.evidence: 24 of 24 Agents SDK sessions signed in silently. With silent SSO blocked, one click on the sign-in button led to an answer in about 20 s.

use_cases.title: Several agents on one page, or one agent per site
use_cases.scenario: A hub page shows an HR agent and an IT agent side by side; each department site shows its own agent.
use_cases.how: Every web part instance has its own connection string and conversation.
use_cases.evidence: Each test page hosted three agent web parts with independent results.

use_cases.title: No host site to open up
use_cases.scenario: A person may use the agent but must not see the agent owner's site. They still chat from their own site.
use_cases.how: The web part calls Copilot Studio directly - there is no `.agent` file or host site in the path.
use_cases.evidence: Shared User C with no access to Site A chatted from Site B. The Agent link (SharePoint channel) blocked the same user.

use_cases.title: Employees without Microsoft 365 Copilot
use_cases.scenario: Employees without a Microsoft 365 Copilot license use the agent; usage is billed to Copilot Studio capacity.
use_cases.how: Standard-harness agents reached through the Agents SDK consume the tenant's Copilot Studio capacity (Copilot Credits).
use_cases.evidence: Every test user had Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) only - no Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Studio license.

use_cases.title: Never reachable anonymously
use_cases.scenario: Security requires that the agent cannot be used without an Entra sign-in, even if a URL leaks.
use_cases.how: Agents SDK endpoints accept only user tokens for `CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke`.
use_cases.evidence: Anonymous calls to both connection strings returned HTTP 401 (re-checked on 7 Oct 2026). The hosted embed of the GitHub Copilot harness agent did not enforce sign-in.

use_cases.title: Update once, every site follows
use_cases.scenario: IT ships a new web part version once and every site gets it; makers publish agent changes without touching pages.
use_cases.how: Tenant app catalog with **Enable this app and add it to all sites**; agent changes go live when the agent is published.
use_cases.evidence: Package 1.0.1.0 -> 1.0.3.0 was rolled out tenant-wide without editing a page; the regression run on Site A passed.

use_cases.title: Answers that respect SharePoint permissions
use_cases.scenario: The agent answers from policy documents in SharePoint and only uses documents the user can read.
use_cases.how: SharePoint knowledge with Microsoft authentication runs generative answers on behalf of the signed-in user (documented for Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft 365 Copilot).
use_cases.evidence: Not tested through the Agents SDK in this engagement - validate before relying on it.

use_cases.title: Agent that knows the page it is on
use_cases.scenario: On a project site the agent already knows the project and tailors its answers.
use_cases.how: Post a custom event with site/page context after the first agent message and read it in an `OnEventActivity` topic (Microsoft Learn pattern). Needs a small web part extension.
use_cases.evidence: Not implemented in this web part yet.

use_cases.title: Same agent in other web apps
use_cases.scenario: The agent is also embedded in a line-of-business portal or a native app with the same sign-in.
use_cases.how: Copilot Studio client library for JavaScript, .NET or Python with the same connection string and a user token (service principal tokens are not supported).
use_cases.evidence: [Integrate with web or native apps](https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-integrate-web-or-native-app-m365-agents-sdk) - not tested here.

tests.title: Silent single sign-on for MFA-protected users
tests.pre: User signed in to SharePoint (MFA satisfied); agent shared with the user.
steps: Open the page with the web part.
Watch the web part while it loads.
tests.expected: The chat connects without a prompt or popup; the footer shows `Microsoft Entra ID SSO · <user>`.
tests.actual: 24 of 24 Agents SDK sessions (12 page loads, 5 personas) connected silently with the user's account in the footer.

tests.title: The agent knows who is chatting
tests.pre: Conversation Start greets with `{System.User.DisplayName}`.
steps: Open the page.
Read the greeting.
tests.expected: The greeting contains the user's display name.
tests.actual: `Hello Agents SDK User A! ...` - every shared tester and the maker were greeted by name on every site.

tests.title: One-click sign-in when silent SSO is blocked
tests.pre: Silent SSO cannot complete (third-party cookies blocked, Conditional Access needing interaction, or an embedding host). Simulated by clearing the MSAL cache and blocking the hidden sign-in frame; two Agents SDK web parts on the page.
steps: Open the page and wait for *Sign in to chat with this agent*.
Select **Sign in with Microsoft** right away.
Complete the popup if prompted, then ask a question.
tests.expected: The popup opens on the first click, the chat connects and answers, and the other agent on the page connects without a second sign-in.
tests.actual: Pass on 1.0.3.0: answer 20.5 s after the click; the second web part reconnected by itself. **Defect found and fixed:** on 1.0.1.0 the first click was blocked by the popup blocker while another web part was still trying silent sign-in.

tests.title: No anonymous access to the agent endpoint
tests.pre: The agent's connection string.
steps: POST to the connection string without an `Authorization` header (command in tutorial step 11).
tests.expected: HTTP 401.
tests.actual: HTTP 401 for Agent A and Agent B (re-checked on 7 Oct 2026).

tests.title: Shared users can chat
tests.pre: Agent shared with the user (End user access), or the user owns it.
steps: Open the page.
Send *Give me one tip for running shorter meetings.*
tests.expected: Greeting and an on-topic answer (`Agent A (standard harness): ...`).
tests.actual: 8 of 8 runs: User A on Sites A-C, User B on Sites A-B, MarioR on Sites A-C.

tests.title: Unshared users are blocked
tests.pre: Agent not shared with the user; the user can open the page.
steps: Open the page.
Send a question.
tests.expected: *You don't have access to talk to this bot, contact the owner.* and no answer.
tests.actual: 4 of 4 runs blocked: User C on Sites B-C, User D on Sites A and C.

tests.title: Removing a user from sharing blocks them
tests.pre: User B is shared and can chat.
steps: Remove User B from the agent's sharing.
Reload the page about 2 minutes later.
tests.expected: The blocked message instead of an answer.
tests.actual: *You don't have access to talk to this bot, contact the owner.*

tests.title: Re-sharing restores access
tests.pre: User B was removed (TC-07).
steps: Share the agent with User B again.
Reload the page.
tests.expected: Greeting by name and an answer.
tests.actual: `Hello Agents SDK User B! ...` and an answer.

tests.title: Access through an Entra security group
tests.pre: Agent shared with a security group; the test user is a member and not shared individually.
steps: Open the page as the member.
Remove the user from the group, wait for the change to apply, reload.
tests.expected: The member can chat; after removal the user is blocked.
tests.actual: Not run - individual sharing was tested. Recommended before go-live because production access should be group-based.

tests.title: Agent sharing and site permissions stay independent
tests.pre: One shared user without site access; one unshared user with site access.
steps: Open the page as the shared user without site access.
Open it as the unshared site member.
tests.expected: 1: SharePoint *You need access* - the web part never loads. 2: The page opens and the agent refuses.
tests.actual: 3 access-denied runs (User B Site C, User C Site A, User D Site B) and 4 agent-blocked runs.

tests.title: One package and one Entra app serve many sites
tests.pre: Web part deployed tenant-wide.
steps: Add the web part with the same connection string on Sites A, B and C.
Open each page as a shared user.
tests.expected: The agent works on every site without per-site app registrations or packages.
tests.actual: Agent A worked on all three sites with one package and one SPA app registration.

tests.title: Visitor (Read) permission is enough
tests.pre: Shared users with Visitor, Member or Owner permission.
steps: Open the page with each permission level.
tests.expected: The chat works for every level.
tests.actual: User A: Visitor (Site A), Member (B), Owner (C). User B: Member (A), Visitor (B). All worked.

tests.title: No host-site dependency
tests.pre: Agent shared with User C, who has no access to Site A.
steps: Open the Site B page as User C.
Ask a question.
tests.expected: The chat works; no access to any other site is needed.
tests.actual: Greeting and answer. The Agent link (SharePoint channel) blocked the same user with *You need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license...*.

tests.title: Several agents on one page
tests.pre: Two or more web parts with different connection strings on one page.
steps: Open the page.
tests.expected: Each web part connects to its own agent and behaves independently.
tests.actual: Every test page hosted three agent web parts; Agent A answered while Agent B returned its harness message.

tests.title: Page opened in Teams, Viva Connections or the mobile app
tests.pre: Applies when these entry points are used.
steps: Open the page inside the host.
Chat.
tests.expected: The chat connects silently, or the one-click sign-in appears and its popup is allowed by the host.
tests.actual: Not run. Embedded hosts can block the hidden sign-in frame or popups - validate before announcing these entry points.

tests.title: Users without Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses
tests.pre: Test users without Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Studio licenses.
steps: Chat as these users.
tests.expected: Chat works.
tests.actual: Every test user had Microsoft 365 E5 (no Teams) only; all shared users chatted.

tests.title: Usage is billed to Copilot Studio capacity
tests.pre: A few completed conversations.
steps: Open the environment's Copilot Studio consumption (Copilot Credits) in the Power Platform admin center.
tests.expected: Agents SDK conversations appear as Copilot Studio consumption.
tests.actual: Not run.

tests.title: GitHub Copilot harness agent through the Agents SDK
tests.pre: Agent built on the GitHub Copilot harness, shared with the user.
steps: Open a page whose web part points to that agent.
tests.expected: Not supported (Microsoft Learn: the client library supports standard-harness agents).
tests.actual: *This action doesn't support agents built with the GitHub Copilot harness.* - 12 of 12 page loads, including the owner.

tests.title: Hosted web chat embed is not an access boundary (comparison)
tests.pre: GitHub Copilot harness agent set to Authenticate with Microsoft, App-channel embed on a page.
steps: Open the page as a user the agent is not shared with.
Open the embed URL in a signed-out browser.
tests.expected: Users without access are refused.
tests.actual: The embed answered unshared users (4 page loads) and a signed-out browser. Use the Agents SDK path for access-controlled agents.

tests.title: A web part update reaches every site
tests.pre: Web part deployed tenant-wide.
steps: Increase the version, rebuild and upload with **Replace** > **Enable app**.
Reload a page on any site.
tests.expected: The new version runs on every site without editing pages.
tests.actual: 1.0.1.0 -> 1.0.2.0 -> 1.0.3.0 on 7 Oct 2026: pages loaded the new bundle right away and the regression run passed.

tests.title: Published agent changes reach every site
tests.pre: Agent in use on several pages.
steps: Change the agent (for example the greeting) and publish.
Select **New chat** on any page.
tests.expected: The next conversation uses the change; no page or package change is needed.
tests.actual: Not run.

tests.title: New chat starts a fresh conversation
tests.pre: An ongoing conversation.
steps: Select **New chat**.
Ask a question.
tests.expected: Transcript cleared, greeting shown again, the agent answers.
tests.actual: Pass on 1.0.3.0.

tests.title: Conversation longer than the token lifetime
tests.pre: A conversation left open for more than about an hour.
steps: Send a message after the access token has expired.
tests.expected: If the message fails, **New chat** signs in again silently and the chat continues.
tests.actual: Not run. Known design limit: the client receives a token, not a token provider.

tests.title: Clear error for a wrong connection string
tests.pre: Web part with a mistyped agent schema name or an unpublished agent.
steps: Open the page.
tests.expected: A readable error, for example *Agent not found (404). Verify the connection string / schema name and that the agent is published.*
tests.actual: Not run.

tests.title: Page context reaches the agent (extension)
tests.pre: Web part extended to post a context event after the first message; `OnEventActivity` topic stores it.
steps: Open the page on a project site.
Ask a project question.
tests.expected: The agent uses the site or page context.
tests.actual: Not run - not implemented in this web part.

tests.title: SharePoint knowledge respects the user's permissions
tests.pre: Applies when the agent uses SharePoint knowledge. User X can read a document, User Y cannot.
steps: Ask X and Y the same question about that document.
tests.expected: X gets a grounded answer; Y gets no content from the document.
tests.actual: Not run through the Agents SDK (documented by Microsoft for Teams, Power Apps and Microsoft 365 Copilot).

tests.title: Guest (B2B) users
tests.pre: Applies when guests use the sites. A guest with page access and agent sharing.
steps: Open the page as the guest.
Chat.
tests.expected: The guest signs in (silently or with one click) and chats if shared; otherwise the agent refuses.
tests.actual: Not run.
